William D. "Bill" Siegel is a New York-based attorney, media executive, and private investor whose relationship with Jeffrey Epstein represents one of the clearest documented examples of a multi-generational Epstein client relationship. His father, Herbert J. Siegel, the billionaire chairman of Chris-Craft Industries, was one of Epstein's original clients during Epstein's tenure at Bear Stearns in the 1980s, alongside Marvin Davis. Bill Siegel served as President and COO of BHC Communications, Chris-Craft's television subsidiary that operated the fifth-largest US station group with 22% household coverage, and as Executive Vice President of Chris-Craft Industries until its .3 billion sale to News Corp in 2001. After leaving the media industry, Siegel became a private investor, neoconservative intellectual, and author of The Control Factor: Our Struggle to See the True Threat (2012), while serving as a trustee of the Hudson Institute and a member of the Council on Foreign Relations.

DOJ Volume 11 documents reveal that Siegel maintained an extensive personal relationship with Epstein from at least 2010 through January 2017 — well into the period following Epstein's 2008 conviction. The documentary record, spanning 57 DugganUSA hits and dozens of EFTA-catalogued emails, shows a pattern of regular in-person meetings in Manhattan (walks near 59th and Madison, meetings at the Apple Store at 767 Fifth Avenue — the same GM Building that housed BHC Communications' former offices), book exchanges at Epstein's 9 East 71st Street residence, repeated offers of Knicks floor seats, and Lesley Groff-mediated phone calls. Siegel also actively expanded Epstein's social network, brokering a meeting between Epstein and Rudy Giuliani in September 2010, introducing London-based Catherine Lurie-Alt in April 2013, and arranging for Epstein to meet Zecharia Sitchin, the ancient astronaut theorist, in May 2010.

Siegel pitched Epstein as an investor in Isbre Holding Corp, a Norwegian glacier water company in which Siegel held a 5.2% stake, sending a 40-page confidential business overview in March 2010 (EFTA02444693). Epstein immediately forwarded the materials to Lyndon Lea, founder of Lion Capital, for evaluation. In January 2015, days after Virginia Giuffre's bombshell allegations in the SDFL filing, Siegel emailed Epstein from St. Maarten dismissing the allegations as "nonsense" and wishing him a happy new year (EFTA02369738). His last documented contact, in January 2017, references mutual friend "Eva" (likely Eva Dubin) and his aging father, who "sends his best" — confirming the tripartite Epstein-Herb-Bill relationship endured across decades. FEC records show Siegel contributed over ,000 to Republican and Trump-aligned political committees through the 2024 cycle.

sections.title: The Chris-Craft Dynasty and Epstein Origins
sections.content:
The Epstein-Siegel relationship traces to the 1980s, when Jeffrey Epstein was building his client base at Bear Stearns. Herbert J. Siegel, Bill's father, was among Epstein's earliest billionaire clients, a fact corroborated by House Oversight documents (HOUSE_OVERSIGHT_023627). Herbert Siegel had amassed his fortune through a series of media deals: Chris-Craft Industries' 30% stake in Warner Communications generated approximately billion when Time merged with Warner in 1989, and the final sale of Chris-Craft to Rupert Murdoch's News Corp in 2001 valued the company at .3 billion. Both Herbert and Bill Siegel appear at hop_distance=1 in the Epstein document explorer entity database, meaning both had direct, independent contact with Epstein — not merely a relationship mediated through one another.

Bill Siegel spent two decades at the heart of the Chris-Craft media empire. He served as President and principal financial officer of BHC Communications (SEC CIK 0000855433), Chris-Craft's Delaware-incorporated television broadcasting subsidiary, and as Executive Vice President and Director of Chris-Craft Industries itself (SEC CIK 0000020067). Year 2000 SEC filings reveal his compensation: ,000 salary, .6 million bonus, ,000 in other compensation, and 437,851 stock options worth approximately .54 million. His brother John C. Siegel held an identical compensation package as EVP. BHC Communications' headquarters at 767 Fifth Avenue — the GM Building — would later become a recurring meeting location with Epstein, who met Siegel at the Apple Store in that same building in April 2013 (EFTA02521088). When Chris-Craft sold to News Corp, BHC minority shareholders challenged the merger in Delaware Chancery Court (In Re BHC Communications Inc Shareholder Litigation, Del. Ch. 2001, 789 A.2d 1), litigation in which Siegel, as BHC president, would have been a central figure.

After the News Corp acquisition, Siegel transitioned to private investment and intellectual pursuits. He operated William Siegel Incorporated as a personal investment vehicle and appeared on Lexington Realty Trust (LXP) earnings calls from 2008 through 2016 as an active shareholder. SEC Form D filings link him to approximately 20 SecondMarket fund vehicles in 2013 and early-stage investments in Mighty Networks Inc and ScaleFactor Inc in 2018. FEC filings variously list his employer as "New Communications Inc," "News Communication," and "BHC Communications" — the latter decades after the company ceased to exist, suggesting either nostalgic self-identification or a successor entity. He was admitted to the California Bar and joined both the Council on Foreign Relations and the Hudson Institute board of trustees.

sections.title: The Epstein Relationship and Social Brokering
sections.content:
The documented Siegel-Epstein relationship spans from at least April 2010 through January 2017, though the Bear Stearns-era family connection suggests contact decades earlier. Communication followed a consistent pattern: Lesley Groff, Epstein's executive assistant, served as the primary scheduling intermediary, relaying call requests, arranging appointments, and confirming meeting logistics. Siegel appeared regularly on Epstein's call lists alongside figures such as Tom Barrack, Jeffrey Leeds, Mort Zuckerman, Amanda Gefter, and Lawrence Krauss (EFTA02422969, EFTA02421344). On September 1, 2010, Groff reminded Epstein that he wanted to speak to "Bill Siegel, woody Merril and JP Molyneux" that day (EFTA02421937) — JP Molyneux being the luxury interior designer, placing Siegel in the same tier of Epstein contacts as high-end personal service providers.

In-person meetings were frequent and casual. In April 2013 alone, Siegel visited Epstein on consecutive days: on April 3, Groff coordinated a 2pm walk, with Siegel "around 59th street and Madison area" asking whether to "walk up to the house" (EFTA02521034); the next day, Groff reported that "the Book from Bill Siegel is on my desk in the Oval Office in a manilla envelope" (EFTA02521550). That same evening, Siegel emailed Epstein: "Great to see you today and we need to talk more." Epstein reciprocated with car rides — in April 2010, Siegel thanked him: "Thanks again for the ride. It was great to see you and I enjoyed our conversation very much" (EFTA02426418). In February 2013, Siegel mentioned visiting Shirley MacLaine's ranch in Santa Fe and "remembered you own half the ranch land there or something," prompting Epstein to describe his Zorro Ranch property (EFTA02521014). Siegel arranged lunches between Epstein and his father Herbert, writing in April 2010: "Let me know some times that work for lunch with my father" (EFTA02426418).

Beyond passive socializing, Siegel actively brokered introductions for Epstein. The most politically significant was a September 2010 effort to arrange a meeting between Epstein and Rudy Giuliani. Groff wrote to Siegel: "Jeffrey wanted you to know he would rather meet with Rudy Giuliani as opposed to his partner this coming Tucs. or Thurs. afternoon. Might it be possible?" Siegel replied that he would try but warned: "Don't expect a quick reply" (EFTA02421673). This took place after Epstein's 2008 conviction, demonstrating that Siegel was willing to leverage his political connections on behalf of a convicted sex offender. Siegel also introduced London-based Catherine Lurie-Alt to Epstein in April 2013, telling Alt "how great you are" and urging Epstein to call her (EFTA02724564). Alt subsequently developed an independent relationship with Epstein that included donations and joint emails cc'ing Siegel (EFTA02679591). Earlier, in May 2010, Siegel had arranged for Epstein to meet Zecharia Sitchin, the author of The 12th Planet and proponent of ancient astronaut theory. Groff noted Sitchin was "in his 90s" and Epstein would send a car (EFTA02424881); Sitchin died five months later.

sections.title: Investment Deal Flow with Epstein
sections.content:
Siegel actively sought to involve Epstein in his investment ventures. The most extensively documented deal was Isbre Holding Corp, a Norwegian glacier water company in which Siegel held a 5.2% stake through Objective/Isbre Holdings LLC (NY DOS 2904499, Delaware LLC, filed May 9, 2003). The parent entity, Objective Investments LLC (NY DOS 2678543), was registered at 555 Madison Avenue, 6th Floor — a prestigious midtown address. On March 31, 2010, Siegel emailed Epstein a 40-page confidential business overview and investor presentation for Isbre, writing: "Forget the other I sent. This is more recent" (EFTA02444692). The pitch deck (EFTA02444693) covered water purity claims of 4 parts per million total dissolved solids, exclusive rights to a Norwegian glacier water source, Tetra Pak packaging, a Bristol, Pennsylvania bottling facility, retail placement strategy, and an Olympic Games marketing angle through Boylan Bottling distribution.

Epstein treated the pitch as actionable deal flow, immediately forwarding Siegel's materials to Lyndon Lea, founder of Lion Capital, a London-based private equity firm specializing in consumer brands — exactly the kind of investor who might evaluate a premium water company. The Isbre venture proved remarkably persistent. The company evolved from Isbre Holding Corp into Isbre Water A/S, which filed a Form D with the SEC in December 2024 (CIK 2046912) for a million offering under Rule 506(c). The executive officer and promoter listed is Mutaz Jafar, based in Ulvik, Norway but reachable at a Kuwaiti phone number (+965-99020008), with placement by Tag Investment Bankers Ltd in London. This Kuwait connection is investigatively significant given Epstein's documented Gulf state network.

Siegel also appeared in the capitalization table of Green Jets Incorporated, an eco-friendly private aviation startup, where he held 14,444 shares (0.9%). The Green Jets balance sheet was forwarded to Epstein on March 30, 2010 by Jennie Saunders, founder of CORE club, via Todd Thomson, the former Citigroup CFO (EFTA02427775). Other notable shareholders included Anja L. Eckbo (13.8%, Norwegian like the Isbre venture), Joseph V. Vittoria (5.3%, former Avis CEO), and Lawrence A. Moens Associates (0.9%, Palm Beach-based). The company carried a negative book value of ,000 with ,000 drawn on a line of credit from Hays Jet Holdings LLC. The overlap between Siegel, Saunders, Thomson, and Epstein in the same cap table confirms a shared deal-flow network among wealthy New York investors, with Epstein positioned as a potential capital source or co-investor.

sections.title: Neoconservative Intellectual Network
sections.content:
Siegel's relationship with Epstein operated along ideological as well as financial channels. His 2012 book, The Control Factor: Our Struggle to See the True Threat (Rowman & Littlefield), argued that Western psychological denial prevented recognition of Islamic extremism. On February 8, 2013, Siegel shared a FrontPage Magazine interview about the book with Epstein (EFTA02521014). The interview, conducted by Jamie Glazov, presented a hardline anti-Islam analysis. Epstein responded warmly: "I already read it. congratulations hope to see you soon." Epstein forwarded and saved the full 14-page interview, suggesting he valued this content enough to archive it. FrontPage Magazine described Siegel as "a lawyer and business executive" who "produces documentary films and assists numerous non-profit organizations" — a reference to his co-production of Road to 9/11 for PBS in 2004.

In April 2010, Siegel forwarded a political article chain to Epstein about US denial of visas to Israeli nuclear scientists from the Dimona reactor (EFTA02426418). The forwarding chain included David Steinmann (likely David J. Steinmann, a neoconservative activist), Minna Elias, Michael Salzhauer, and Morry Kalimian (a major NYC real estate figure). This email chain reveals Siegel's embeddedness in pro-Israel and neoconservative policy circles that overlapped significantly with Epstein's own network of contacts. A separate three-way email with Epstein and an unidentified "paula" in May 2013 (EFTA02569425) prompted Siegel to reply "HAH! or should I say UGH! I will send to Peter as to" — the political tone and distribution pattern suggesting shared commentary on current events.

Siegel's institutional affiliations reinforced these connections. As a trustee of the Hudson Institute, he sat alongside Marie-Josee Kravis (wife of KKR's Henry Kravis and vice chair of the Hudson board), Richard Perle (the neoconservative foreign policy architect), Susan M. Steinhardt (likely wife of hedge fund pioneer Michael Steinhardt, who had his own Epstein connections), Dan Quayle, and Nina Rosenwald (intelligence-linked philanthropist). Herbert London, Hudson's president, endorsed Siegel's book. The Hudson Institute's board thus constituted a nexus of think-tank governance, Republican donor networks, and financial industry connections that paralleled the social infrastructure through which Epstein maintained his post-conviction access to elite circles. Siegel appeared on Peggy Siegel's August 2010 guest list for a Wall Street screening event, paired with Monica Crowley, the Fox News commentator and later Trump administration figure. He was tagged as "BUSINESS" with connections to "NEWSCORP/NEWS AMER/CRISCRAFT," placing him at social events alongside Leon Black, David Koch, Robert Wood Johnson, and Maria Bartiromo (EFTA02424126).

sections.title: Post-Scandal Loyalty
sections.content:
The most revealing aspect of Siegel's relationship with Epstein is its durability after Epstein's legal troubles became public knowledge. On January 3, 2015 — four days after Virginia Giuffre's explosive filing in the Southern District of Florida naming prominent individuals — Siegel emailed Epstein from St. Maarten: "Just read the post article and wanted to wish you a happy new year and send a wish 2015 gets all this nonsense behind you. Let's get together some time" (EFTA02369738). The characterization of victim allegations as "nonsense," sent from a Caribbean vacation destination in the same region as Epstein's island properties, captured both the dismissiveness of Epstein's social circle toward the allegations and the continued social normalcy of the relationship.

Two years later, on January 12, 2017, Epstein and Siegel exchanged another warm communication. Epstein wrote: "she and you shared some fun stories. how are you." Siegel's response referenced "Eva" — likely Eva Dubin or Eva Andersson-Dubin — describing a "JE love festival" and writing: "When you are in ny let's grab lunch or dinner, with or without Eva. Miss seeing you." He added: "Just saw my father who sends his best. He is getting up there" (EFTA02338194). This final documented exchange confirms the tripartite relationship endured: Herbert Siegel, the original Bear Stearns-era client, still sending his regards to Epstein through his son; Bill, still socializing with Epstein and their mutual friend Eva; and Epstein, still embedded in the social fabric of a billionaire media dynasty decades after the original financial client relationship was established. The January 2017 date is significant — it places the active friendship at less than two and a half years before Epstein's final arrest in July 2019.

His primary employer entity, variously reported to the FEC as New Communications Inc, News Communications Inc, or News Communication, has not been located in SEC EDGAR filings or in the corporate registries of Florida, New York, New Mexico, Pennsylvania, the USVI, the United Kingdom, or the Cayman Islands. No Deutsche Bank transaction records involving Siegel have been found in the DS10 dataset. No FAA aircraft registrations, FARA foreign agent filings, UCC liens, NYC ACRIS property records, or OpenSanctions hits match William D. Siegel. Notably, for a corporate executive who oversaw a major media merger, zero federal court cases have been found naming him personally — suggesting either effective use of corporate counsel shielding or sealed proceedings.
